prompts.surface: Generate one 16:9 scientific hypothetical local-terrain illustration of Callisto, Jupiter's outer Galilean moon. Independent original scene, no source/reference image, do not reuse or recolour Moon/Mars/Pluto/Io/Europa/Ganymede maps. Eye-level close view of an invented heavily impact-weathered icy-rocky landscape, rounded crumbling light grey ice-rich knobby hummocks with dark dusty low areas, sparse small worn craters and angular fragments, large scale landscape receding to low horizon, black airless sky. Research context Galileo2001 shows bright knobs and dark low areas, but sublimation/dust movement and exact chemistry are hypotheses; depict no active eruption, plume, exposed ocean, biology, astronauts or survivable landing. Material fractions, all particular terrain forms, composition, colour, illumination and exposure are invented; understated grey-brown dusty appearance rather than blue transparent glacier. Sun outside frame, directional low light, no other celestial body. Visually lucid broad shapes with modest detail, natural cinematic science illustration, no text/captions/grid/borders. Canvas exactly wide16:9.
prompts.sky: Generate one original 16:9 hypothetical observer illustration from Callisto's Jupiter-facing hemisphere, independent scene no reference images or analog skins. Black tenuous-exosphere sky occupies upper two thirds; invented grey-brown dusty heavily weathered icy-rocky knobby hummocks and scattered fragments across lower third, no blue transparent glacier. Exact bands, colour, phase, orientation, exposure and lighting imagined, not photometry or dated ephemeris. Keep disc small specified width, not dominant giantplanet. Sun outside view at representative5.2044AU; no other planets, rings, dense stars, moons or suns. No plume, exposed ocean, biology, astronauts, spacecraft, surviving landing implication.
